title: QBR Insight Lab — Preflight & Facilitator Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, scenario-driven QBR facilitation playbook intended for CS leads running 60–90 minute strategic QBRs. Focus: drive decisions for renewal, unblock technical issues, and align exec-level stakeholders.

Intended audience:
- CS Manager / QBR facilitator (owner)
- Account Exec (shadow / decision owner)
- Solutions Engineer (technical lane)
- Customer stakeholders (product, eng, ops, procurement)

High-level approach (Insight Lab):
- Preflight data snapshot + 2 x scenario ladders (Neutral, Upside, At-risk)
- Timebox discovery, highlight wins, validate risks, drive 1–2 concrete decisions
- Use ‘decision cards’ to capture asks and owners in realtime

Preflight checklist (48–72h before):
- Pull usage metrics: monthly active users, tokens/day, peak latency windows, error rate by route (owner: SE)
- Business KPIs: feature adoption rates, A/B flags, revenue run-rate impact (owner: AE)
- Support surface: top-10 recent tickets, P0/P1 incidents last 90d (owner: CS Ops)
- Health indicators snapshot: adoption, latency, cost-per-call delta, infra incidents (owner: facilitator)
- Exec readiness: confirm sponsor(s), ask for pre-read + any open procurement deadlines
- Logistics: meeting platform link, recording permission, live doc link, slide-less mode recommended
- Pre-meeting ask: request customer to share 1 slide of priority goals (optional)

Artifact checklist to attach to meeting invite:
- 2-page pre-read: usage + top issues + agenda
- Live Google doc for decisions + action log
- Technical appendix (KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, quantization notes)

Agenda — 90 minute (modular lanes for 60m):
- 0:00–0:05 Host & objectives (facilitator) — set success criteria for this QBR
- 0:05–0:20 Customer goals + top wins since last QBR (customer speaks) — tripwire: call out any missed commitments
- 0:20–0:35 Data snapshot (facilitator) — adoption, latency, costs, incidents; highlight 3 signals
- 0:35–0:50 Technical deep-dive lane (SE) — show root cause for top incident or ops friction (if none, run mini-runbook)
- 0:50–1:05 Scenario ladders & recommended plays (facilitator + AE) — 3 scenarios with explicit asks
- 1:05–1:20 Decision forum (execs + AE) — pick 1 primary renewal outcome and 1 technical sprint owner
- 1:20–1:30 Wrap, next steps, assign owners, confirm follow-up cadence

Facilitator script snippets (editable during meeting):
- Opening: "Thanks all — objective for today is to confirm 1 renewal decision path and align on one technical unblock we can ship in the next 30 days. If we hit that, we call the meeting a success."
- When walking data: "Here are three signals we think matter most for your use case; tell me which one you disagree with and why."
- If conversation stalls on pricing: "Let's park pricing and decide the technical scope that changes adoption — pricing follows impact. We have 7 minutes for a quick decision exercise."
- For risk: "We see this as a high-risk item because it prevents X users; what's one immediate action we can commit to within 2 weeks?"

Scenario ladders (run during 10–15m segment):
- Neutral (baseline): usage steady, no critical incidents, renewal recommendation: standard renewal. Asks: 1) small adoption playbook (30d), 2) schedule post-renewal follow-up.
- Upside (growth): clear adoption velocity and exec sponsor engaged. Asks: 1) commit to reserved capacity pilot, 2) roadmap alignment session.
- At-risk (declining usage / unresolved tech debt): asks: 1) 30d remediation sprint (SE owner), 2) limited-term discount + success milestones, 3) weekly progress sync for 60 days.

Decision card template (one per ask) — capture in live doc:
- Decision title
- Outcome options (e.g., standard renewal / conditional renewal / non-renewal)
- Primary owner (name + role)
- Success metrics (quantified where possible)
- Due date
- Dependencies/risks

Renewal risk rubric (quick 0–10 scoring):
- Adoption health (0–3): low active usage = 3 risk
- Technical health (0–3): unresolved P0/P1 or performance > target = 3 risk
- Sponsor strength (0–2): executive sponsor active = 0, absent = 2
- Contract runway (0–2): <30 days = 2, 30–90 = 1, >90 = 0
Total >=6 => high risk (trigger escalation to CS leadership)

Technical playbook lane (if SE needed):
- Quick triage pattern: reproduce -> isolate component -> mitigation -> patch plan
- Common remedies we can propose live: increase batching, pin model variant, enable prefix caching, add fallback model for latency spikes
- Ask: include proposed change and an estimated delta (latency/cost/QL) in the decision card

Playbook for difficult dynamics (executive absent / procurement pressure / competitive bidding):
- Executive absent: pause renewal talk; schedule a 20m skip-level with sponsor OR close with conditional renewal (30d technical sprint + milestone)
- Procurement pressure: capture exact asks and timelines; convert to decision card and propose staged commitment (e.g., pilot -> reserved capacity)
- Competitive RFP: map feature gap vs competitor; propose short-term bridge (API extension / custom eval) and 14-day proof-of-value

Follow-up templates (post QBR email skeleton):
Subject: QBR summary + decisions — [Account] — [date]
Hi [Sponsor],
Thanks for the time today. Attached is the 2-page summary. Key decisions:
- Decision 1: [title] — owner: [name], due: [date]
- Decision 2: [title] — owner: [name], due: [date]
Next steps: we will run weekly 30-min check-ins until milestones complete. Meeting notes & action items: [link to live doc]

Decision tracker column hints (for live doc):
- id, decision_title, owner, status (open/in-progress/blocked/done), score (impact 1–5), due_date, linked_ticket (JIRA), notes

Parking lot and escalation rules:
- Items > 5 dependencies -> escalate and spin up a focused engineering triage outside QBR
- If renewal risk rubric >=6, notify CS Director AND AE director within 24 hours

Notes-to-self (fragments / quick edits):
- Consider adding a one-pager that translates latency improvements to revenue impact (finance-friendly language)
- Validate that caching proposal doesn't invalidate customer compliance constraints (ask security)
- Try a 60m version for smaller accounts: trim technical lane -> collect offline

Unresolved questions (to resolve pre-call if possible):
- Do we have a live dashboard for prefix cache hit rate by customer? (SE)
- Which internal owner will ship the remediation if accepted? (product/infra?)

Appendix (links & quick refs):
- Pre-read template: /templates/qbr-two-page-pre-read.md
- Decision board sample (sheet): shared_drives/customer-success/qbr-decision-board-sample.csv
- Recent incident log: shared_drives/customer-success/customer-incident-log-Jan-Feb-2025.csv

End of doc — lightweight, intentionally modular. Use this as a runbook and adapt language for customer tone.
